facts.fact: On Datasanté's page a community doctor at Matielona, sole general practitioner for about 12,000 people, states that since using a tablet linked by wifi to her solar-powered Datasantébox she keeps no paper register and everything is in each patient's computerised record, held on the local server; she received the equipment in November 2019 and speaks after several years of use. The page is undated, so the published date is used.

A study presented by Dr Diamondra Mandimbimalala on Datasanté's page covers 35 community doctors (25 private, 10 public) trained and equipped with Datasanté: 10 use the software regularly and 20 irregularly; 12 have created more than 1,000 patient records, 6 between 500 and 1,000, and 12 fewer than 500. The count is of doctors, not facilities, there is no denominator, and the study is undated, so the published date is used.

Datasanté's page describes the software as used by community general practitioners, first-line doctors in isolated rural practice, 25 of the 35 equipped being private and 10 public; it says the 2019 server-client version will also be offered to public basic health centres (CSB), which is a proposal and not a deployment. The page is undated, so the published date is used.

Datasanté's page presents the network as run by Datasanté with the community doctors' association AMC-MAD, a volunteer pilot programme dating from early 2010 with equipment handed to doctors in full ownership; among the study's perspectives is to conclude an agreement with the health ministry, which implies none existed. The page is undated, so the published date is used.

Datasanté's page states that it is seeking partnerships between actors of the North and Malagasy general practitioners to finance the equipment (Datasantébox server, battery, tablet, mobile solar panel), supplied to participating doctors without per diem; no state funding is mentioned. The plan is described as for 2019.

systems.platform: Datasanté (single-PC version from 2010; server-client Datasantébox with tablets from 2019)
systems.owner: Datasanté with AMC-MAD (Association des Médecins Communautaires de Madagascar)
systems.tiers: rural community doctors' practices: 35 doctors equipped (25 private, 10 public); to be offered to public CSB

note: The software also produces the monthly activity report (RMA): 17 of the 35 doctors send reports (8 daily, 5 irregularly, 4 by hand at meetings) and 18 send none. That is the EMR feeding routine reporting and gives no hmis fact, the system being of class emr. Dates in the body are mixed (programme from 2010, plans for 2019, equipment in November 2019, testimony some years later).
